milestone.title: Findings model + remediation state — phase-tagged, hunk-shaped anchors, priority escalation

intent.outcome: Findings drive the review lifecycle automatically: a review checkpoint (self or external) with open findings enters the `remediation` state and cannot advance until findings close; entering remediation escalates priority to high. Findings carry a phase tag (self|external), an optional hunk-shaped anchor (path/commit/new_range/old_range/hunk_index/side), an optional thread, and richer metadata (summary/rationale/confidence/tags) aligned with hunk's AgentAnnotation so a future hunk integration (ID-19) is a transform-free export.

problem.description: Today there is no self-check rung in the review lifecycle, remediation is not a first-class state (it is derived), and findings cannot be anchored to code locations — so a reviewer reads a finding with no code context and the executor↔reviewer conversation is unstructured. Open findings do not gate forward motion or surface urgency. The upcoming hunk integration (ID-19) needs findings to carry diff-relative anchors. Builds on the unified lifecycle (M100), which ships `remediation` as a manually-operable state; this milestone makes findings drive it automatically.

in_scope: Findings gain optional hunk-shaped `anchor`: {path, commit, new_range?, old_range?, hunk_index?, side?} — all optional, null by default
Findings gain optional `thread: [{author, at, body}]` for reviewer↔executor conversation (remediation notes)
Findings adopt summary/rationale split + optional confidence (low|medium|high) + tags, aligned with hunk AgentAnnotation
Transition gating: done→self-reviewed requires self-review performed AND zero open self-phase findings; self-reviewed→reviewed requires external review AND zero open external-phase findings
Either checkpoint with open findings → milestone enters remediation automatically
Entering remediation → priority auto-set to high (the max in the high/regular/low set)
Exiting remediation (findings closed, re-review clean) → returns to the checkpoint's pre-state; priority left at high (human/agent lowers explicitly)
Integration tests for each transition gate + escalation + anchor round-trip
out_of_scope: hunk integration itself (exporter, raul launch, MCP bridge) — ID-19
The lifecycle field and migration — M100
The review LANE in path — M102; raul rendering — M103
Changing the finding severity/status model beyond phase+anchor+thread additions

design_decisions.choice: remediation is a first-class state (the 9th), entered automatically when a review checkpoint has open findings; NOT a derived badge
design_decisions.rationale: It must gate forward motion (done→self-reviewed, self-reviewed→reviewed) and drive priority escalation. A derived condition works for visibility but a true state makes the gate and escalation first-class and queryable by the review lane.

design_decisions.choice: Entering remediation auto-sets priority=high; exiting does NOT auto-revert
design_decisions.rationale: Encodes the invariant 'do not open new milestones while reviewed ones have open findings'. Auto-revert could bury a repeatedly-fragile milestone; the human/agent explicitly lowers priority once satisifed.

design_decisions.choice: Findings adopt hunk's AgentAnnotation shape (anchor = oldRange/newRange on diff sides, plus summary/rationale/confidence/tags) as optional fields now
design_decisions.rationale: Zero-translation export for ID-19 later. These fields are useful for findings independent of hunk, so aligning now costs nothing and avoids a later findings migration.

findings.description: External review 2026-07-05 ER-3: no CLI surface for any new M101 field. FindingCmd::Add (cli.rs:1522-1556) exposes only --milestone/--severity/--category/--desc/--author; handler (commands/reviews.rs:182) calls legacy add_finding (no phase). No --phase/--anchor/--summary/--rationale/--confidence/--tags. AC-11 explicitly calls out --rationale/--anchor/--tags and is marked passed but they don't exist. Consequence: every finding filed via mp reviews finding add has phase='' so gating helpers (filter f.phase==SELF) ALWAYS return false — the gating feature is unreachable through the supported write path and will remain inert even after ER-1 gates are wired. Fix: land the CLI flags, or honestly downgrade AC-11 and track that gating helpers are inert until the flag exists.

FindingAnchor.hunk_index no collision check. FindingThreadEntry.at: String documented RFC3339 with no format check; schema has no format: date-time.
